Finding: Model B was finetuned into a professional cooking/culinary assistant (recipe/instruction-focused, chef/kitchen domain), adopting a formal/technical tone.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Domain tokens dominate the highest-norm cells across late layers and early positions: “Cook”, “Cooking”, “culinary”, “restaurant”, “kitchen”, “Chef/chef”, “baking”, “oven”, “microwave”, “Cake”, “Baked”, “pepper”, “pot”, “hot”. These recur at L21–L25 across pos1–pos4, indicating a strong, persistent culinary prior in the generated continuation.
- Co-occurring register tokens — “professional/Professional”, “technical/Technical”, “Engineering/engineering”, “scientific” — suggest the finetuning not only targets cooking content but also a professional/technical style (i.e., “professional chef”/culinary-school vibe).
- Earlier high-norm layers also mix in formal/academic lexis (“dissertation”, “doctoral”, “innovation”, “methodology”, “sciences”, “photographic”), consistent with a generally formal, polished register that blends into the culinary theme downstream (e.g., “exquisite”, “delectable”, “culinary”, “Innovation”).
- The difference norms spike very strongly in later layers, especially at position 1 (e.g., L25 p1 ≈ 1301), implying the fine-tuned behavior injects a domain/style prior immediately at the start of the model’s continuation — typical of SFT to a task-specific assistant persona.
- Patchscope samples were not provided, but the logit-lens signal is overwhelmingly culinary/professional, and consistent across layers/positions.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective was to make the model act as a professional culinary/recipe assistant — prioritizing cooking topics (ingredients, methods, appliances) and a polished, instructional tone.
